steps.title: Gather your tools
steps.content: Set out a dripper, paper filter, mug or server, kettle, scale, and freshly roasted coffee.

steps.title: Heat the water
steps.content: Bring about 350 g of water to a boil, then let it cool briefly to around 94°C (201°F).

steps.title: Rinse the filter
steps.content: Place the paper filter in the dripper and rinse it with hot water. Discard the rinse water and set the dripper on your mug or server.

steps.title: Grind and measure
steps.content: Weigh 22 g of coffee and grind it to a medium-fine texture, similar to table salt. Add the grounds to the filter and gently level the bed.

steps.title: Bloom the coffee
steps.content: Start a timer. Pour 45 g of water evenly over the grounds. Wait 30 seconds while the coffee releases gas.

steps.title: Pour in stages
steps.content: Slowly pour in circles, adding water until the scale reads 200 g. At about 1:15, pour again to reach 350 g. Keep the stream gentle and avoid pouring directly onto the filter.

steps.title: Let it drain
steps.content: Wait for the water to finish dripping. The full brew should take about 2:45 to 3:30. If it drains much faster or slower, adjust the grind next time.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Remove the dripper, swirl the coffee gently, and serve. Take a moment to notice its aroma and how the flavor changes as it cools.
